registration_statement: Committed alone, before any bid_source_guard implementation (Rust or Python) and before docs/bid/bid_source_manifest_v1.json exists. Never edited after commit: a changed case, expectation, code or decision rule is acceptance_v2, and cases are never weakened after a failure.

governing_records.sections: sec. 3 (RM-OQ-11: terminal package state 2de86ab, technical source 5eee4b8, lineage b5849af -> 2de86ab; any later change needs a new explicit owner decision)

work_packages SC-WP-12 (admission_criteria: fails on every preregistered tamper case, passes on the recorded lineage; fails on any docs/bid/** byte change after 2de86ab without a new explicit owner decision record); first_execution_sequence ES-1

manifest.only_new_path_under_docs_bid: the manifest is the only path under docs/bid/ that is not a file of the terminal package state
required_content: technical_source: commit, root tree id, and sha256 / bytes of every file at the technical source that the package cites (the tests/test_bid_package.py::_cited_paths rule) or that the package builder reads (source_facts.Source.text during build_package.build_all)
package_lineage: b5849af then 2de86ab, each with its docs/bid tree id and the sha256 / bytes of every docs/bid file at that commit, and its authorising decision records
terminal_package_state: 2de86ab; the protected file set is the terminal lineage entry's file map
migration_state_at_freeze: every component python-authoritative; Kernel 1 admitted as an optional backend with DEFAULT_BACKEND 'python'
manifest.generation: generated once from git objects at the lineage commits and the technical source; it is not trusted: the history part re-derives every recorded tree id, file set, sha256 and byte count from git

implementations.rust_primary: crates/abep-provenance/src/bid_guard.rs (abep_provenance::bid_guard); git is used only for the history part, through std::process::Command
implementations.python_while_python_ci_exists: scripts/ci_checks.py check `bid_source_guard` (a 12th check; the 11 existing checks are unchanged); it reads the same manifest
implementations.ci: ci.yml integrity job (fetch-depth 0) runs the Python check; the Rust guard runs in cargo test and in a full-history Rust workflow step

parts.files: reads only the working tree (docs/bid/**, the mission scenario, the manifest); needs no git
parts.history: needs a full-history git repository; evaluated against `head` (default HEAD)

semantics.overall: FAIL if either part is FAIL; otherwise NOT_EVALUATED if the history part is NOT_EVALUATED; PASS only if both parts are PASS. NOT_EVALUATED is never a pass: the Rust CLI exits non-zero and the Python check reports a problem

governed_constants.rule: compiled into both implementations from CLAUDE.md / A9.29 sec. 3; the manifest must record exactly these values

files_part.check: the manifest parses, has schema abep_bid_source_manifest_v1 and every required field with the registered types (40-hex commits / tree ids, 64-hex sha256)

manifest technical_source.commit, terminal_package_state.commit, the ordered package_lineage commits, mission_scenario_v2 path / sha256 and manifest_path equal the governed constants, and the terminal state is the last lineage entry
every expected file (terminal lineage file map, adjusted only by valid owner authorizations) exists in the working tree
every expected file has the recorded sha256 (and byte count where recorded)
every file entry under docs/bid/ is an expected file, the manifest itself, or matches an ignored generated-artifact pattern; an authorized REMOVE path that exists is unlisted
docs/bid/bid_technical_baseline_v2.json exists, parses and its bid_technical_source.commit equals the governed technical source
every owner_change_authorizations entry is valid (below); an invalid entry grants nothing

history_part.check: a git repository is given and `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints false; otherwise the part is NOT_EVALUATED and no further H check runs
the technical source, every lineage commit, the terminal state and the head resolve to commits; otherwise FAIL and no further H check runs
technical source is an ancestor of lineage[0]; lineage[i] is an ancestor of lineage[i+1]; the terminal state is an ancestor of the head (git merge-base --is-ancestor; a commit is its own ancestor)
the technical source's root tree id and each lineage commit's docs/bid tree id equal the recorded ones
at each lineage commit, the docs/bid file set equals the recorded file map and each blob's sha256 / bytes equal the recorded ones
every recorded technical-source file exists at the technical source with the recorded sha256 / bytes

the head's committed docs/bid equals the expected state: every expected file present with the expected sha256 (else BID_FILE_MISSING / BID_FILE_MODIFIED), no other committed path except the manifest (else BID_FILE_UNLISTED); ignore patterns do not apply to committed files
the head's committed config/mission/mission_scenario_v2.json has the governed sha256
any other git failure inside a full-history repository

ignored_generated_artifacts.rule: a regular file whose parent directory is named __pycache__ and whose name ends in .pyc, in the working tree only (gitignored Python bytecode written when tests import docs/bid/package/*.py); nothing else is ignored

changes.sha256_after: 64-hex for MODIFY / ADD; absent for REMOVE

valid_iff: decision_record.path starts with docs/decisions/OD_, the file exists and its sha256 matches
every change path is under docs/bid/ and is not the manifest
MODIFY / REMOVE name a protected file; ADD names a non-protected path
sha256_after is 64-hex for MODIFY / ADD and absent for REMOVE
no path is named twice across all entries
owner_change_authorizations.effect: a valid entry replaces the expected state of exactly its paths (MODIFY / ADD: sha256_after; REMOVE: absent); an invalid entry is reported and changes nothing

finding_codes.manifest_invalid_rule: an invalid manifest fails both parts with MANIFEST_INVALID and no other check runs

tree.REPOSITORY: the repository working tree itself, evaluated in place (read only)
tree.COPY: a fresh temporary directory holding copies of the terminal lineage files, the manifest and config/mission/mission_scenario_v2.json from the repository working tree, then the tamper operations applied in order

history.REPOSITORY: the repository the acceptance runs in (full history required)
history.SCRATCH_SHALLOW: a depth-1 clone (git clone --depth 1 file://...) of a temporary two-commit repository
history.SCRATCH_FULL: a temporary two-commit repository with full history that does not contain the lineage

acceptance_cases.head: HEAD, or the full commit id given

operations.append_bytes: append the hex-decoded bytes to path
operations.create: write text (UTF-8) to path, creating parent directories
operations.replace_all: replace every occurrence of old by new in the UTF-8 text of path
operations.manifest_set: set the RFC 6901 pointer in the copied manifest to value (manifest re-serialized)
operations.manifest_reverse: reverse the array at the RFC 6901 pointer in the copied manifest

decision_rules.per_case: for each case and each implementation: overall, files and history equal the expected values; every required code is reported in its part; a part expected PASS reports no finding
decision_rules.agreement: for every case the Rust and Python implementations report the same overall / files / history results and the same set of finding codes per part
decision_rules.verdict: ACCEPTED iff every case meets per_case in both implementations and agreement holds; otherwise NOT_ACCEPTED
decision_rules.not_run: the acceptance run needs a full-history repository; in a shallow clone it refuses (NOT_RUN_HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE) instead of scoring
decision_rules.once: the acceptance run is executed once for v1 at a recorded commit and its report is committed whatever the verdict; after NOT_ACCEPTED only a code fix plus acceptance_v2 may follow (no case is removed or weakened)
decision_rules.development: cargo test and pytest execute the same cases on every run as regression tests; those runs are not the acceptance report

admission: on ACCEPTED, NI-BID-SOURCE-GUARD is recorded ADMITTED in docs/rust_migration/migration_state_v1.json with the report as admission evidence, a docs/HISTORY.md entry and the CI jobs
what_this_is_not: not physics and not a gate verdict: it protects the frozen bid record only
not a re-freeze: the bid record stays 5eee4b8 / 2de86ab; only a new explicit owner decision can authorize a change (owner_change_authorizations)
